title: cohere --json
description: One line of `cohere --json`: newline-delimited JSON, one object per line, told apart by `kind`. Findings and changed files come first, in any order; the summary is always the last line, so a reader that never sees one knows the run did not finish.

finding.description: One finding: a rule's, or a type error, whose rule is its TypeScript code (TS2322).

path.description: The file, as an absolute path.

rule.description: The rule's name, or the TypeScript code for a type error.

messageId.description: Which of the rule's messages this is. Absent for a type error.

changedFile.description: One file the run rewrote, by fixing or by formatting.

rules.description: The rules whose fixes were applied, for a fixed file.

engineBuild.description: An engine a development cohere built from source before it could check, its sources or the toolchain having changed. Its time is not in the summary's seconds, which are the check's alone. A released cohere builds nothing.

engine.description: The binary built, such as cohere-swift.

key.description: The cache key it was built under, the hash its binary is named by.

ignoreEntry.description: One entry of the root settings' ignorePatterns, or one of cohere's defaults, as this run's discovery counted it.

reason.description: Why the paths are never checked. Absent when none was given.

kind.description: What the paths are. Absent when none was given.

check.description: A check that still reads the paths. Absent when none was named.

file.description: The settings file that wrote the entry, as an absolute path, or the set's name, such as cohere:next, or cohere for one of its defaults.

default.description: One of cohere's defaults, written by no settings file: testdata, which the Go engine and the format walk never enter, and Vendor, which the format walk and the Swift engine never enter. Each holds only there, so a file a tsconfig includes under either is still type-checked and linted, and neither is ever a finding. Absent for an entry a settings file or set wrote.

matched.description: The paths it matched, files and directories it takes whole, among every entry of every directory discovery read before any ignore applied, inside repositories of their own too, and, for an entry the walk found nothing for, at and below the path it names. Zero for an entry a settings file wrote, unless its kind is generated, is a finding, correctness-no-unused-ignore, which fails the run.

ignorePatterns.description: The root settings' ignorePatterns, in a run of several projects, whose summaries are each a project's: the list a run of one carries on its summary. Written once, before the projects' lines.

crash.description: A rule that could not finish a file, or a file nothing could check, because cohere crashed. A bug in cohere, not in the code checked, and it fails the run.

rule.description: The rule that crashed. Absent when the whole file was lost.

cause.description: The panic, as cohere caught it.

timing.description: What a Go run's CPU went to, under --timing: the Go engine's timing record, written through once before the summary. Every CPU figure is microseconds of the kernel's thread clock read on a thread held for the work, so none is wall time, and each has the measuring's own cost taken out. What the rows leave of processCpuMicroseconds is what no row measures, never spread over them. A run that is not Go, or not under --timing, writes none.

unavailable.description: Why no CPU was measured, when the thread clock cannot be read. Every CPU figure is then 0 and means nothing; the counts are still real. Absent when the CPU was measured.

processCpuMicroseconds.description: The engine process's user and system CPU from its start to the record.

load.description: The load's phases, each summed across the goroutines that ran it, so each runs past the load's wall.

listCpuMicroseconds.description: This process's own CPU listing the packages.

listChildrenCpuMicroseconds.description: The CPU of the go commands the listing ran, its children's, which processCpuMicroseconds does not hold.

exportDataPackages.description: Packages whose types were read from export data in place of their source.

rules.description: One entry for each rule that ran, most expensive first, summed over every package and build. Empty when no rule ran.

packages.description: Packages the rule's analyzer ran on, dependencies analyzed for facts included.

calls.description: Calls a dispatcher made into the rule's listener, 0 for a rule that walks on its own.

shared.description: The analyzers no single rule owns, most expensive first. Empty when none ran.

name.description: The analyzer's name, buildir for staticcheck's intermediate representation build.

kind.description: An intermediate representation build, staticcheck's or the engine's own; a dispatcher's walk less its calls into the listeners, which are billed to their rules; or another analyzer several rules read.

measuredCalls.description: Pieces of work measured, each costing two reads of the clock.

measuringCpuMicroseconds.description: What those reads cost, already taken out of the rows.

duplicate.description: Under --duplicates: two or more functions whose canonical IR is one graph, size 11 and up, one idea written more than once. A report, never a finding: it moves no count of the summary and never its verdict.

size.description: The instructions that compute something, the smallest member's, in the engine's own IR.

digest.description: The canonical hash the members share, in hex.

path.description: The file, as an absolute path.

kept.description: The reason a suppression gives for keeping this function in its shape. A group is written while one member is not kept.

duplicateRefused.description: Under --duplicates: a function the hash could not read faithfully, refused by name rather than guessed past.

detail.description: The syntax kind or instruction, where the reason needs one.

duplicateCoverage.description: Under --duplicates, always once, after the report's other lines: what it looked at, what it left out and what it cost, or why it did not run, so its absence is never read as no duplicates.

notRun.description: Why the report did not run, when it did not.

floor.description: The size from which a group is written.

filesIgnored.description: Files the settings ignore, left out.

functions.description: Every function looked at: hashed, refused and not read.

refused.description: Refused functions by reason, each listed as a duplicateRefused line.

notRead.description: Functions never read, by reason: bodyless, generated, or copied (a file marked cohere:copied, which every house rule withholds too).

withheld.description: Groups at the floor whose every member a suppression keeps.

deadSuppressions.description: Suppressions naming the report's rule that keep no member of a group at the floor. Listed, never findings, while the report is not a gate.

crashes.description: Files, or packages by their first file, the hash could not read at all.

summary.description: The run, the last line. `verdict` is what the exit code says; `gaps` is every way the run fell short of checking everything, which a reader deciding whether a passing run can be trusted reads too.

schemaVersion.description: Raised by any change a reader could notice; a new optional field does not raise it.

label.description: The project's path, in a repository with several projects.

error.description: Why the run stopped before it could judge anything, such as a tsconfig that does not load, in the words the human view prints. Present only then, and the verdict is fail.

ignorePatterns.description: The root settings' ignorePatterns, then cohere's defaults, when the run discovered its project. findings counts each dead one, an entry a settings file wrote that matched nothing and whose kind is not generated.

graphSeconds.description: Reading, parsing and binding the program; zero when no graph was built.

formattingSeconds.description: The part of the fix phase's seconds with a format in flight; the fix phase's seconds include it. Absent when no formatter ran.

replayed.description: The run was answered whole from the run cache, and ran no phase.

filesReplayed.description: Files whose findings came from the cache: in a run that computed the rest, those it did not; in a whole replay, every file in scope. Zero only when no file's findings came from the cache.

missReason.description: Why a run the cache could have answered whole was not: no run on record for these arguments, a key and which of its parts moved (the cohere binary, the project root, the arguments, the configuration), or the input that changed. Absent when it was answered whole or reads no cache.

findingsMissReason.description: Why files' findings were not replayed: none on record, a key and which of its parts moved, or how many files had no entry, changed bytes or rules, or were taken without measuring readiness. Absent when every file looked up was replayed.

memoryRaisedToBytes.description: Each limit a Go run raised its heap to after its load, in bytes and in the order raised. Absent when it raised none, from a replay, which started no engine, and for every other run.

packageCache.description: What the Go engine's per-package findings cache did in the lint phase, by package. Present only for a Go run that linted, and absent from a replay, which started no engine.

on.description: False under `--no-cache`, and then every count is zero but standardLibraryFromBinary, factsSkipped and reloads.

hit.description: Packages restored from an entry, with nothing run on them.

standardLibraryFromBinary.description: Go standard-library packages restored from the entries a release binary carries, with nothing run on them, apart from hit. `--no-cache` reads them too. Absent when zero.

written.description: Missed packages that got an entry.

unstorable.description: Missed packages that held a fact no entry can hold.

factsDropped.description: Facts the written entries left out, since nothing outside their package can name their object.

factsSkipped.description: Restored facts skipped, whose object the package's export data does not hold.

waves.description: Times the lint phase analyzed packages, at most two: those whose own inputs moved, then the rest that missed once the early cutoff restored what it could above them.

reloads.description: Packages loaded again from source, though the cache held them, because a rule asked of a fact computed on demand that no entry answered, so the lint phase ran again. Absent when zero.

reloadRounds.description: Times the lint phase loaded and ran again for those reloads, each round loading every package the last one needed. Absent when zero.

replays.description: Questions of a fact computed on demand that the lint phase answered by replaying the push's walk of a package, with the cache or without. Absent when zero.

problems.description: What kept the cache from being read or written, every build's, each said on stderr too: keys that could not be computed, an entry that could not be encoded, a write that failed. It never changes a finding. Absent when zero.

writeFailed.description: Entries whose write failed, every build's. Stderr and problems say only the first, so this is how many the store refused. Absent when zero.

builds.description: Every build a Go run checked when it checked more than one, since some file of the project compiles only for another platform, the host's first. Its findings are the merge of every build's. Absent for a run of one build and every other run. A replay keeps it, since the verdict it repeats was merged from these builds.

target.description: The build as `GOOS/GOARCH`, with ` cgo` when cgo is on and its tags after ` tags `: `darwin/arm64 cgo`, `windows/arm64`.

host.description: The host's build, which is the first.

compiledFiles.description: The project's files the build compiles.

analyzedPackages.description: The packages the build analyzed: every root for the host's, and for another only those that could find what the host's did not.

findingsAdded.description: Findings that stand which this build reported and the host's did not. Zero for the host's.

findingsDropped.description: Findings this build reported that the merge left out, since their rule keeps only what every build with a say on the file reports.

entriesKept.description: The host's alone: the packages its build kept an entry of for the other builds to restore from. Absent when 0.

restoredFromHost.description: The packages this build restored from the host's run rather than checked: its own findings cache did not hold them, their own inputs were the host's, and everything they read of other packages read the same here. Absent when 0.

declinedAtLoad.description: The packages this build's load checked from source after all, since what they read of other packages' types did not hold here. Absent when 0.

declinedAtCheck.description: The packages this build's check declined, since what they read of other packages' facts or answers did not hold here, which had the build loaded again. Absent when 0.

declinedBy.description: Each decline, and each package never restored from the host's run, by why: ownInputs, noHostEntry, neverRestorable, readsUnknown, exportData, typeReads, lookups, factReads, deprecations or answers. Absent when empty.

reloadRounds.description: How many times this build was loaded again, for the packages its check declined or for a package a question reached restored with no answer of it kept. Absent when 0.

reloadRoundsBy.description: Each time this build was loaded again, under every reason it had: hostDecline or missingAnswer. Absent when empty.

writtenThrough.description: The packages this build restored from the host's run whose entry it wrote to its own findings cache once their restore held, so its next run hits them there rather than check them from source. Absent when 0, and always under --no-cache, which writes nothing.

loadMilliseconds.description: This build's wall time loading the workspace, every reload included. Absent when 0.

lintMilliseconds.description: This build's wall time running the rules, every reload included. Absent when 0.

decideMilliseconds.description: An extra build's time deciding which packages restore from the host's run, summed across the goroutines that decided, so it can exceed the load and lint it ran within. Absent when 0.

keepMilliseconds.description: The host's alone: its time keeping its packages for the other builds, within its lint: their keys, which a run without a store computes only for this, and what each entry holds of the run's answers, since the entries themselves are encoded when a build first asks for them. Absent when 0.

waitMilliseconds.description: The host's alone: how long the other builds waited after its lint for its walks of what each package read of others to end, before any could start. Absent when 0.

checkedFromSource.description: Another build's alone: the packages of its whole graph its loads checked from source rather than restored, summed over every load, a reload's included. Its first load's count over packagesLoaded is the share that weighs its lint, which lints alone at or above one half. Absent when 0.

checkedFromSourceRounds.description: Another build's alone, written only when it was loaded more than once: the packages each of its loads checked from source, the first's then each reload's, which checkedFromSource sums. Absent otherwise.

packagesLoaded.description: Another build's alone: every package its first load loaded, dependencies and test variants included. Absent for the host's.

lintWaitMilliseconds.description: Another build's alone: how long its lint waited for its weight of the budget of one build the builds share, admitted in the order they became ready. Absent when 0.

lintWaited.description: Another build's alone: whether its lint waited for its weight at all, so a wait under a millisecond still reads as one. Absent when it did not.

filesAlone.description: Files of ours in scope that only this build compiles and that a rule ran on: the coverage it buys. Absent when 0.

notLinted.description: Files of ours in scope the host's build leaves out that this build, the first to compile them, compiled and no build analyzed, absolute and sorted. Each is also in gaps.unchecked, as not linted. Absent when none.

notLintedReason.description: Why no rule ran on notLinted: a build whose load found a type error analyzes no package. Absent when notLinted is.

buildsAtOnce.description: How many of the builds beside the host's ran side by side, decided once as they started from the machine's cores, the memory cap and the live heap. It changes no finding: the builds' results are merged in the order of builds whatever it is. Absent when builds is, and kept by a replay with them.

buildsWidthLiveBytes.description: The host's live heap, in bytes, buildsAtOnce was decided from, measured by a collection once the host's reads were whole. Absent when the decision needed none: one build at a time under --single-threaded or a limit other than the cap, builds that restore nothing from the host, or too few cores or builds for more than one at a time.

findings.description: Rule findings, type errors not included.

wouldChange.description: Under `--no-fix`, the files a fix or formatting would rewrite, the nested repositories' included, each a finding line. They fail the run.

nestedWouldChange.description: The part of wouldChange in nested repositories: files their own run would rewrite. Absent when zero.

wouldChangeConsidered.description: Under `--no-fix`, the files the fix phase examined, the scope wouldChange less nestedWouldChange was found in. Absent when zero.

nestedWouldChangeConsidered.description: The nested repositories' files the formatter read, the scope nestedWouldChange was found in. Absent when zero.

cohered.description: The files the run rewrote, fixed or formatted: the `fixed` and `formatted` lines' files, each once.

filesInScope.description: Every file the run was to account for: checked plus cached.

checked.description: The files examined fresh this run.

cached.description: The files the cache answered for.

typesOnly.description: The files an ignorePatterns entry naming "check": "types" matched, beside filesInScope and not in it: type-checked, their type errors reported, and never linted or formatted. Absent when there were none. A file only plain entries match is in no count, since it is never checked at all.

nodes.description: The syntax nodes walked this run, in the checked files.

programFiles.description: The program's size when the run was narrowed to fewer of its files; zero otherwise.

crashedFiles.description: Files nothing could check, because cohere crashed on them. They fail the run.

ruleCrashes.description: Rules that crashed on a file, each leaving its verdict there missing. They fail the run.

path.description: The file, as the engine names it.

rule.description: The rule that crashed. Absent when the whole file was lost.

cause.description: The panic, as cohere caught it.

crashes.description: Each crash crashedFiles and ruleCrashes count, named, so the list is as long as the two together. The same fields as a `crash` line, which a Swift run does not print. Absent when there are none.

rulesSkippingEverything.description: Rules that declined every file they were offered.

nothingToCheck.description: The project had no files to check.

sourceFiles.description: How many files of its language the project held before anything kept one out of a check: a TypeScript program's own files, or the files an engine's project counts in its package. Present only when nothingToCheck is set and the project had such files. It is what a run that checked nothing fails on; excluded is its explanation, and files no reason counted are named there as unrecorded.

reason.description: Why the files were left out, in the words the footer prints, such as `ignored by git`.

count.description: How many files this reason left out.

source.description: The first rule that decided, as `path:line` relative to the project root, such as `.gitignore:1`. Absent where no rule did, as for a narrowing.

excluded.description: Why each file of a run that checked nothing was left out, one entry per reason. Present only when nothingToCheck is set and the project had files of its language: such a run fails, since it checked nothing. A project with no file of its language at all has none, and passes with the warning alone.

indexFallback.description: Why a format walk read no tracked path from its repository's index: a split or sparse index, one git did not write, or none yet. The walk decided by the ignore files alone, so a file git tracks under a pattern that matches it went unformatted, counted ignored. Absent when the index was read or the root is in no repository.

modifiedBuild.description: The binary was built from a modified tree, so no commit reproduces these findings.

unread.description: Files the run could not check for any other reason, as the run said it.

nestedUnread.description: Why the nested repositories could not be read for drift. Their files are never the run's to check, so the run went on. Absent when they were read.

phasesNotRun.description: The check's phases the run has no record of, because it stopped before them, such as a run that formatted and never type-checked or linted. Absent when every phase was reached.

adamicIgnored.description: Adamic .a files the program holds that git's ignore rules leave out of the format walk: type-checked and linted, never formatted. Absent when there are none.

nestedUnchecked.description: Files in the nested repositories the run reads that the formatter could not check, each named in the account. A gap, never the verdict: the nested repository's own run fails on them. Absent when there are none.

missingGenerated.description: Generated files the program asks for that do not exist yet, relative to the project root: an import or reference path in a project file whose target git ignores, such as Next's .next/types before `next typegen`. They fail the run. Absent when there are none.

fixesHeld.description: Lint fixes were held because an input the program was told to load is missing: a generated file, or an import, reference or types entry that resolves to nothing. None was proposed or written, and formatting ran alone. Absent otherwise.

file.description: The file, as the engine names it.

reason.description: Why the engine left it out, in the engine's words, such as "no target of this package compiles it" or "excluded by build constraints on darwin/arm64".

language.description: The language of the engine that left it out, "Swift" or "Go", which the footer counts it in: "3 Swift files not checked".

unchecked.description: Files an engine's run listed as not checked for a reason other than the ones nobody expects checked. In a Swift run those are git ignoring them, Vendor/ or being a package manifest, so this today means no target of the package compiles them and they are no standalone script the run checks alone (a file of declarations only, or a script whose imports name two platforms), less those under a Swift project below it that runs on its own. In a Go run the expected reasons are git ignoring them and, under --other-builds, another build having checked the file ("checked by the windows/arm64 build"). So without the switch this means a file only another platform builds, or one that imports "C" while cgo is off, since the Go engine then checks the host's build alone, and with it only a file no build the run checked compiles. Each is listed, however many share a reason. They fail nothing. Absent when there are none.

file.description: The file, as the engine reached it under the root.

realPath.description: Where the file really is, every symbolic link resolved: outside the root.

notWritten.description: Files a fix phase, TypeScript's or an engine's, would have written and did not, since each is reached through a symbolic link to a real path outside the root. A fix never writes another project's files: each was checked, its findings stand, and its fixes were withheld. The run is incomplete. Absent when there are none.

changedDuringRun.description: Files whose text changed between the fix phase's walk and its fix, under another agent or an editor's save. The walk's fixes for each were refused, since their offsets point into bytes the file no longer holds, and asked for again against the text it holds; its findings describe the text the walk read. The run is incomplete, and is never replayed. Absent when there are none.

package.description: The dependency's package, as the Go engine names it, such as "net".

file.description: The file, as the Go engine names it.

errors.description: The type errors withheld in it.

withheldInDependencyCgo.description: Files of a dependency with cgo files whose type errors a Go run withheld, because no cgo tool ran and the faked package "C" is what they are about, sorted by file. They are a dependency's, not the project's to fix, so they fail nothing. Absent when there are none, as on macOS.

withheldDependencyCgoDeclarations.description: Declarations of dependencies with cgo files that every rule of a Go run was given without their bodies or initial values, because no cgo tool ran. They fail nothing. Absent when there are none, as on macOS.

swift.description: What only a Swift run says of itself. Absent for every other run, and for a Swift run with nothing here to say.

sdkIndexSeed.description: What the check of the standalone scripts did with the toolchain's SDK index seed (#f6pqraj): its key, the name of its folder under ~/Library/Caches/cohere/sdk-index, and whether the run's empty index store was seeded from it rather than indexing the SDK afresh. Absent when the check's store was not empty or no seed applied.

adamic.description: Adamic readiness: the files whose types are true, with no type error and no cohere:adamic finding before suppression, whatever the project's rules enable. Present only under --adamic-readiness, and then always: a run that asked and could not measure it says so.

reason.description: Why readiness was not measured, in a clause; present only when it was not.

files.description: The files the lint walk measured or tried to.

ready.description: The files with no type error and no cohere:adamic finding.

unmeasured.description: Files a cohere:adamic rule skipped for a missing precondition, or the cache replayed without a count. Never counted ready.

optionsMissing.description: The compiler options Adamic sets that the project's tsconfig leaves off, so the files were measured under weaker options than Adamic's.

failingFilesByRule.description: By cohere:adamic rule, the files it found something in.
